issues.legal_issue: Temporary cultivators alike in relevant respects cannot be treated differently in permanent land allotment solely because their temporary leases began in different periods without a rational connection to the allotment objective.
material_facts: The government established separate permanent-allotment regimes for temporary cultivators whose leases began before and after a cutoff.
The earlier-lease group could receive land up to a higher limit, while the later-lease group could be denied further allotment once its existing holding crossed a lower limit.
Both groups’ temporary leases were cancelled, and neither group could acquire tenancy rights in the leased land.
The record did not establish how long before the cutoff the earlier leases had begun, and the difference in occupation length did not justify the different allotment treatment.
An earlier allotment scheme had not distinguished between the two groups.
issues.conclusion: The temporal distinction had no rational nexus to the allotment objective. The definition of a landless person in Rule 2(1)(xiii) and Rule 3(2) of the post-cutoff rules were discriminatory and void under Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 requires a classification to rest on an intelligible basis with a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved. Sections 15 and 15A of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act did not support the distinction: the proviso to section 15 and section 15A excluded tenancy rights for both groups. Sections 7 and 28 of the Rajasthan Colonisation Act provided the framework for allotment and rulemaking but did not make the groups legally different for this purpose. The court also referred to State v. Ramdhan, AIR 1973 Raj 71, which had struck down rules that treated the family unit differently under allotment schemes made under the same Act.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_land_allotment_rules and allotment_terms_varied_by_lease_period and both_groups_lacked_tenancy_rights and duration_evidence_missing

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_allotme: The proceeding challenged government rules governing permanent allotment of land on equality grounds.
predicates.allotment_terms_varied_by_lease_period: The government prescribed different allotment eligibility or amounts for temporary cultivators according to when their leases began.
predicates.both_groups_lacked_tenancy_rights: The law prevented both groups of temporary cultivators from acquiring tenancy rights in the leased land.
predicates.duration_evidence_missing: The record did not establish a relevant difference in the length of occupation that could explain the different treatment.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns land-allotment rules, the allotment terms vary by lease period, both groups lack tenancy rights, and relevant duration evidence is missing, the temporal classification is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Allotment conditions cannot provide materially different benefits to temporary cultivators based on the size of their existing holdings without a rational basis.
material_facts: Under the earlier-lease conditions, a cultivator with more than the basic allotment could retain land up to the ceiling and pay for land above the basic allotment.
A cultivator with less than the basic allotment could receive additional land only to reach the basic allotment and had to pay for the newly allotted land.
The court found no justification for the difference in treatment between cultivators with holdings above and below the basic allotment threshold.
issues.conclusion: Condition No. 3 of the earlier-lease conditions was discriminatory and void under Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits arbitrary differences in treatment between persons within the relevant class; a classification must have a rational nexus to its objective. The court relied on this equality principle in assessing Condition No. 3. Sections 7 and 28 of the Rajasthan Colonisation Act authorized land grants and rules but did not justify the unequal treatment.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_allotme: The proceeding challenged government rules governing permanent allotment of land on equality grounds.
predicates.allotment_benefits_varied_by_existing_ho: The allotment conditions gave cultivators different retention or additional-allotment benefits according to the size of their existing holdings.
predicates.no_basis_for_holding_threshold: The government offered no justification for the difference in treatment based on the existing-holding threshold.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge concerns land-allotment rules, benefits vary by existing holding, and no basis supports that threshold, the holding-based allotment condition is invalid.
